function: CNN classifies the best K-of-N transmit antenna subarray for THz-ISAC hybrid beamforming from channel and target-response inputs; hybrid beamformers computed by manifold optimization (pp. 7, 9).
system: THz ISAC BS with N = 32 to 128 antennas, K = 8 selected, 8 RF chains, 16 subcarriers; 16-antenna user, 3 targets; no RIS (pp. 4, 9).
method: CNN classifier (13 layers) mapping channel and target responses to the best subarray index; supervised with labels from model-based Algorithm 2; cross-entropy, SGD with momentum (pp. 9, 11).
data_channel: Custom simulated THz multipath channel (path gains with molecular absorption), random angles in [30, 150] degrees; 480,000 samples, 70% training, 30% validation for testing (pp. 4, 11).
test_conditions: Train: noisy samples at 15/20/25 dB SNR (N = 32, K = 8, G = 4); test: held-out 30% with SNR_TEST swept -10 to 10 dB (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Model-based Algorithm 2 (search over subarrays, G = 1, 2, 4), random subarray with and without BSC, fully digital full-array beamformer; no other learned antenna-selection method compared (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Spectral efficiency versus SNR, K, RF chains and epsilon; antenna-selection accuracy; number of subarray configurations; computation time in seconds (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Computation times in seconds (Tables I-II, p. 12): CNN 0.037 s versus model-based 0.287 to 269.441 s; complexity order O(N_iter K^2 N_RF M N_ds) for beamformer (p. 7).
q1_support: p. 4: "we assume a general scenario, wherein the THz channel matrix H[m] includes the contribution of L multipath scatterers"; custom THz model (Eqs. 4-6) with no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "The validation dataset is then used for testing the CNN model after it is corrupted by synthetic noise"; held-out data of the same set with an SNR sweep (Fig. 10b), one configuration N = 32, K = 8, G = 4, no new scenario or array.
q3_support: p. 12: "CNN-based antenna selection yields (about 2%) higher SE than the model-based approach in Algorithm 2"; the comparators are non-learned (Algorithm 2, random subarrays on p. 10), and no earlier learned method (refs [19], [43]-[46], p. 3) is simulated.
q4_support: p. 12: "COMPUTATION TIMES (IN SECONDS)" Tables I-II report the learning-based selection at 0.037 s versus 0.287 to 269.441 s for the model-based search; p. 7 gives the complexity order of the beamformer optimization.
q5_support: p. 11: "The training dataset D is generated for I1 = 1000 different data realizations"; a self-generated synthetic dataset, and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Area 5: the learned part is antenna selection of a THz ISAC array serving a communication user and T = 3 targets; the CNN only picks the subarray, the hybrid beamformers come from model-based manifold optimization (Algorithm 1, p. 7). Antenna selection is read as an array-resource decision of the ISAC beamforming, not antenna hardware design: reviewer to confirm the function check. Only spectral efficiency is reported, with sensing entering through the target-response input and the weight epsilon (p. 6). Carrier frequency and bandwidth are not given in Section IV. PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (arXiv:2307.07242v1); the DOI is not printed in the file.
